transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, yeah, I came in because... honestly, things have been a bit much ever since my father-in-law moved in with us. He brought so much stuff with him, you wouldn't believe it. We had to stack boxes all the way to the ceiling in the garage, which completely blocked my workbench. He's got this massive collection of old ceramic mugs from every state he's ever visited. I think he's only missing Idaho and maybe Alaska, but he insists on displaying them all in the kitchen now. 

But anyway, ever since he got settled in, I've just been... well, I’m holding it together at work just fine. I’m an EMT, so you kind of have to compartmentalize, you know? Just yesterday we had a call for a guy who slipped off a ladder and dislocated his shoulder, and you just go into autopilot. You don't even think about it, you just do the job. My partner, Dave, he always gets a little squeamish with joints, but I've seen it a hundred times. 

But at home? And with this bachelor's coursework I'm trying to finish up? I’m just way more wound up and short-tempered than I’m used to being. I snap over nothing. And I don't even have the patience for the things that usually keep my head clear anymore. I've been completely skipping my fishing trips, haven't done any woodworking... I even stopped going to the community first-aid workshops I usually help out with. So, yeah, I just haven't been myself.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time lately?

No, not depressed really. I mean, I don't feel hopeless or anything like that. Just... wound up, like I said. It's more of a frustration thing, you know? Like, I try to sit down and do my coursework, and I can hear my father-in-law in the other room watching his game shows. He watches them on max volume because his hearing aids are "uncomfortable." I tried telling him, I said, "Frank, they make different earpieces for those now, we could go to the audiologist," but he won't hear of it. He says the audiologist down on Elm Street—the one next to the old bakery that closed down last year, such a shame, they had the best bear claws—anyway, he says that guy doesn't know what he's doing. So instead, I get to listen to the Price is Right through two walls. But yeah, no, I wouldn't say I'm depressed. Just... ready to snap sometimes.
Have you found that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you normally like?

Well, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. It's not like that. Like, I still *want* to do my woodworking, you know? If I could actually get to my workbench, I'd be out there right now. I was in the middle of making this really nice oak coffee table before Frank moved in. Oak is just fantastic to work with. It's heavy, sure, but it takes a stain beautifully. 

My partner Dave at work, he's actually trying to build a patio deck out of untreated pine right now, and I told him, I said, "Dave, that pine is going to warp before the summer's over." He wanted to borrow my cordless circular saw for it—it's a Dewalt, great battery life on that thing, highly recommend it—but I had to tell him I couldn't even reach it because it's buried behind about forty boxes of Frank's old National Geographic magazines. Seriously, who drags magazines from 1984 across the state? They weigh an absolute ton. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, no, I still enjoy my hobbies. I just... I'm too keyed up to sit still for them right now, or I literally just can't get to my tools.
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or run down lately, even if you haven't been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Tired? No, not really. I mean, working EMS you're always a baseline level of tired just from the shifts, but nothing out of the ordinary. Actually, speaking of things being run down, we had to take one of the ambulances, Rig 4, into the shop last week because the alternator was whining. Sounded exactly like a dying cat every time you stepped on the gas. 

The mechanic over at the county garage—this guy Sal, great guy, he actually makes his own venison jerky—he was telling me the fleet manager is buying cheap aftermarket parts again to save a buck. Which is just ridiculous, because when you're running lights and sirens down Route 9 in the middle of the night, you cannot have your electrical system bog down on you. Sal's jerky was fantastic, by the way. A little heavy on the black pepper, maybe, but really good. He hunts up near the state line, says the deer up there are getting huge because of the mild winters. 

But wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, am I feeling tired. No, physically I'm fine. I've got plenty of energy, honestly, it's just all nervous energy right now with Frank in the house.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than usual, or feeling anxious about things even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Anxious? Worrying? No, not really. I mean, there's always a reason when I'm stressed, you know? Like right now, it's Frank. It's not just out of nowhere. I don't sit around worrying about the sky falling or anything. 

Speaking of falling, though, we had a call just yesterday—elderly woman took a spill down her front steps. Nasty fracture on her tibia. We had to traction splint it right there on the lawn. Her neighbor, this guy in a bathrobe, comes running over, and I swear to you, he's holding a spatula. Like, what are you going to do with a spatula, buddy? Flip her leg back into place? People do the weirdest things when they panic. Turns out he was making pancakes when he saw her fall through the window. Blueberry pancakes, he said. Which, honestly, sounded pretty good. I haven't had a good pancake since that diner on 4th Street closed down. They used to make them the size of hubcaps. 

But no, I don't worry about random things. I just... I get stressed about the actual things in front of me. Like the fact that I have zero space in my own house right now.
Would you say you've been more irritable or prone to anger recently, even over small things?

Irritable? Yeah, well, I guess so. I mean, that's kind of why I came in here. Ever since Frank, my father-in-law, moved in with us, I've just been really short with everyone. I manage to hold it together at work—you have to in EMS, obviously—but at home, or when I'm trying to get my coursework done, I'm just so wound up. 

Actually, speaking of coursework, I'm taking this online class for advanced trauma life support, right? And the platform they use for the videos is just garbage. It buffers every two minutes. My internet provider is supposed to be giving us gigabit speeds, but I swear, they throttle it during peak hours. I called them up last week, and this guy on the phone—sounded like he was eating chips or something while he was talking to me—tried to tell me it was my router. I said, "Buddy, I have a mesh network set up, it's not the router." Mesh networks are great, by the way, if you have dead zones in your house. I set one up for my sister last year in her colonial, and it works perfectly. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. Being irritable. Yeah, I've been short-tempered at home. And I've even started skipping the things that usually help me blow off steam, you know? Like my woodworking, obviously, because of the boxes, but I've also been skipping fishing, and even those first-aid workshops I usually help run. I just... I don't have the patience for it right now.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately, like trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you’re tired?

Sleep? No, I've actually been sleeping fine. When I finally get to bed, I'm out. Working the shifts I do, your body just kind of learns to shut down when it has the chance, you know? 

Although, speaking of shutting down, my truck's battery died on me two days ago right in the driveway. Just completely dead. I had to get my neighbor, Dave, to give me a jump. Dave's a good guy, he's got this massive Ford F-250. Thing is practically a tank. He uses it to tow his boat down to the lake on weekends. He's got a nice little pontoon, actually, we went out on it a couple of times last summer. Caught some decent bass, too. The trick with bass around here is you gotta use those soft plastic lures, the ones that look like little crayfish. The fish go absolutely crazy for them right around dusk. 

But yeah, no, sleep isn't really an issue for me. Once my head hits the pillow, I'm asleep.
